passages.original: 6 suam agnoscit. Erii proinde Zeno tractatuum in pt. cævm auctor declarandus. Qui enim illos conscripsit, prœdictam prœfationem generalem non semel in iis memorat ut propriam. Hallucinatus est igitur Cassiodorus, qui hanc prœfationem Hilarii nomine laudat. Erravit el Augustinus, qui tractatus in ps. cæVIII, toties cum lib. de Nat. et Gral. tum contra Julian. non Zenoni,sed Hilario attribuit. Erravit Hincmarus, errarunt el alii, quotquot Hilarii in psalmos testimonio se uti existimarunt, cum Zenonis verba in medium proferrent.
passages.english: ... acknowledges [it] as his own. Zeno will therefore have to be declared the author of the tractates on Psalm 118. For the one who wrote them mentions the aforesaid general preface in them more than once as his own. Cassiodorus therefore was mistaken, who cites this preface under the name of Hilary. Augustine too erred, who so often attributed the tractates on Psalm 118, both in the book On Nature and Grace and against Julian, not to Zeno but to Hilary. Hincmar erred, and others erred too, as many as supposed they were using the testimony of Hilary on the Psalms, when they were bringing forward the words of Zeno.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence: "6 suam agnoscit" continues "prologi n." in the preceding context, presumably "prologi n. 6" ("in section 6 of the prologue [the author] acknowledges as his own"). "in pt. cævm" and "in ps. cæVIII" are read as scanning errors for "in ps. CXVIII" (Psalm 118, Vulgate numbering; Psalm 119 in Hebrew numbering). Other scanning errors corrected: "Erii" for "Erit", "el" for "et", "Gral." for "Grat." (De Natura et Gratia). This is an editor's argument, which the following context goes on to qualify.
